Subject: Re: Quick onboarding smoke test — p99 spikes / timeouts

Jordan —

During our automated onboarding smoke tests this morning we saw repeated p99 latency spikes (12–18s) and occasional timeouts at peak concurrency (~40 req/s). This started around 08:45 UTC and persisted intermittently for ~40 minutes. The integration is basic (single-stream text generation) so this is surprising.

I attached a short log sample and a screenshot from our synthetic test harness. Two notes:
- The bursts line up with autoscaler decisions in our logs (new GPU node creation)
- We’re on the hosted API; we did not request any special throughput.

FinOpt is trying a live pilot next week so this is blocking. Can your team confirm whether this is an onboarding configuration issue or a platform-side regression? We need an ETA and mitigation plan.

Thanks,
Sara

Subject: Re: Quick onboarding smoke test — p99 spikes / timeouts (initial findings)

Quick summary of what I’m seeing from the autoscaler and runtime traces (logs attached: autoscaler-trace-20270605.txt):
- Timeline: a traffic surge began 08:43 UTC. Autoscaler triggered 5 new GPU nodes. Provision time observed: 75–140s (p50=82s, p95=118s, p99=139s).
- Root contributors to provisioning lag:
  1) Container image pulls were rate-limited by the regional artifact registry (we saw repeated 429s while pulling large model artifacts).
  2) NV driver + CUDA module init on freshly provisioned nodes added ~20–30s of cold-driver overhead.
  3) Model weight mmap/deserialize for the large quantized weights incurred an additional 20–60s depending on concurrency and IO path.
- Result: streaming requests that hit a node still in the "initializing" state were queued or retried at the client level, producing elevated p95/p99 and a small number of 504s.

Mitigation options (short-term):
A) Add a small standby pool (2–3 GPUs) pre-warmed with the onboarding model for FinOpt pilot hours (costed). This would remove the image-pull + driver cold-path for the majority of bursts.
B) Use a lightweight fallback model (smaller variant) automatically when backend nodes report INIT state, returning degraded-but-fast results while the full model finishes loading.
C) Adjust autoscaler aggressiveness / increase concurrency thresholds to reduce node churn.

I recommend A + B for the next 48–72 hours while we fix registry throttling: standby pool during the pilot window + temporary fallback model.

Action items:
- Rachel: correlate distributed traces to verify whether client-side retries are contributing to amplified traffic. Deliverable: trace correlation and request timeline.
- Prioyom: confirm whether product can enable model fallback gating by config flag for this customer.
- Marissa/Jordan: approve standby pool and communicate costs/credits to customer.

-Sean
SEAN GALLAGHER
SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: autoscaler-trace-20270605.txt

Subject: Re: Quick onboarding smoke test — p99 spikes / timeouts

Sara — thank you for the sample and patience. Jordan looped us in and Sean shared an initial technical read. We agree this looks like a cold-path provisioning issue on our side (registry throttles + node init). We own this.

Immediate proposals (short window / low-friction):
1) Standby warm pool: we can enable 2 GPUs warmed with the FinOpt onboarding model during your pilot windows (we estimate this will reduce p99 below 3s for the majority of requests). Cost: we can absorb 50% of the standby cost for the first 72 hours as a goodwill credit.
2) Short-term fallback: enable the smaller quantized variant automatically for requests routed to initializing nodes; quality delta is minor for the test harness and reduces latency dramatically.
3) Engineering fix: Sean’s team will work with infra to change registry pullbackoff and prefetch artifacts to avoid 429s; ETA for registry change: 24–48 hours.

Can you confirm pilot test windows (local timezone) and whether FinOpt is ok with the temporary fallback model? If yes, we’ll schedule standby activation and push the config toggle.

Apologies again — we’ll keep you updated every 2 hours until the pilot finishes.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
